newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PENGUINS FIRE JOHNSTON AS COACH, GM PATRICK TAKES OVER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PENGUINS FIRE JOHNSTON AS COACH, GM PATRICK TAKES OVER.

text.p: The Pittsburgh Penguins, losers of eight of their last nine games, fired head coach Eddie Johnston on Monday and named general manager Craig Patrick the coach for the rest of the season.
The 60-year-old Johnston, serving in his second stint as Penguins coach, will be reassigned to another position in the organisation, the NHL club said.

The Penguins have dropped four games in a row to fall nine points behind first-place Buffalo in the Northeast Division. Pittsburgh is 31-26-5 and currently the fifth seed in the Eastern Conference, two points ahead of the New York Rangers.

Pittsburgh won the Northeast Division championship last season with a 49-29-4 record (102 points) last season, but were beaten by the Florida Panthers in the Eastern Conference championship series, four games to three.

Johnston had a 153-98-25 record since taking over in 1993. He previously coached the Penguins for three years from 1980-81 to 1982-83 and was promoted to the general manager position in May of 1983, a position he held for five seasons.
Johnston's overall record as Penguins coach is 232-224-60.
The 50-year-old Patrick has served as general manager since December 1989. He also served as the team's interim coach for the rest of that season.

Patrick has made numerous trades during the season in an effort to improve the team, but the club seems to have regressed. Patrick acquired defencemen Darius Kasparaitis and Fredrik Olausson, centres Stu Barnes and Greg Johnson and left wing Garry Valk since the start of the season.
To make matters worse for the struggling Penguins, star right wing Jaromir Jagr may be sidelined for at least another month with a recurring groin injury.
